title: Practical Inference Tuning Cheat Sheet - Draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic cheat-sheet for engineers and SREs who need fast, repeatable tuning guidance for reducing inference cost while meeting latency SLOs. It synthesizes recent experiments across chat, completion, and embeddings workloads and gives concrete starting knobs for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization choices. Not a spec — a working set of heuristics engineers can apply in prod experiments and tune from there.

How to use this doc:
- Pick the workload profile that most closely matches your traffic (chat short/long, streaming, embedding, rerank).
- Apply the recommended default knobs under "Quick starts".
- Run 1–2 A/B experiments vs baseline for 24–72 hours and check cost/latency/quality deltas.
- Use the "experiment log" template below to capture results.

Quick starts (by workload)
1) Small interactive chat (median input ~120 tokens, response ~80 tokens, p95 latency requirement < 300ms):
   - Batch size target: 2–4 concurrent requests per device for CPU-bound small GPUs; 4–8 for high-throughput GPUs (A100/H100).
   - Max batching delay: 8–12ms (aim for low additional queuing latency).
   - KV/prefix cache: enable request prefix caching for repeated system prompts + transient user personalization; TTL 30s for chat sessions, invalidate on model switch.
   - Quantization: prefer fp16 or bf16 if available for quality-sensitive flows; int8/awq as an experiment only when quality budget > 1–2% relative BLEU/perplexity.
   - Expected unit improvement: 20–45% cost drop with negligible p95 impact if batching tuned properly.

2) Long-context generation (documents, summarization, 4k–32k tokens):
   - Batch size target: 1–2 (memory is usually limiting).
   - KV caching: critical — use streaming KV-cache checkpointing so repeated prefixes aren't recomputed. Cache retention per-session: keep whole session for up to 10 minutes or until memory pressure triggers eviction.
   - Quantization: fp16 recommended; awq-int8 reduces memory but watch for hallucination regressions — run QA evals.
   - Offload: enable CPU KV offload if model supports and latency SLO allows 50–120ms additional per-token.
   - Expected unit improvement: q8 + cache can reduce token compute by 2.5–4x vs naive CPU serving.

3) Embeddings (short fixed inputs, high QPS, latency SLO < 50ms):
   - Batch size target: large (16–64) depending on GPU memory; micro-batching and pipelined copies recommended.
   - Use synchronous batching with prefetch and prioritized small requests to avoid head-of-line blocking.
   - Quantization: int8/4-bit often safe for embeddings; validate cosine-distance drift on representative corpus.
   - Cache: local per-worker LRU of recent embedding vectors (TTL 1–5m) for repeated queries.
   - Expected unit improvement: batching + q8 can reduce cost per vector by 60%+.

4) Reranking / multi-stage (candidate generation + rerank):
   - Strategy: keep generation stage high-throughput cheap model; rerank with smaller quantized model where possible.
   - Batch size: rerank batch = number of candidates x requests; pack candidates into single forward if supported.
   - Quantization: aggressive (int4/ternary) on reranker often acceptable; validate precision@k.

Concrete knob table (spreadsheet-friendly rows)
- Column headers suggested: workload, model family, baseline qconfig, recommended qconfig, battarget, max_queue_ms, cache_policy, expected_cost_delta
- Example rows (text bullets here for portability):
  * small-chat, Llama-2-13B, fp16 baseline, recommend: fp16 -> awq8 (if quality budget), battarget 4, max_queue_ms 10, cache_policy session-prefix-30s, expected_cost_delta -30%
  * long-gen, Falcon-40B, fp16 baseline, recommend: fp16 with KV-checkpoint + q8 experiments, battarget 1, max_queue_ms 20, cache_policy full-session-10m, expected_cost_delta -45% (with offload)
  * embeddings, combiner-2B, fp32 baseline, recommend: q4 -> int8 pipeline, battarget 32, max_queue_ms 50, cache_policy recent-embed-5m, expected_cost_delta -65%

Quality guardrails and monitoring
- Always run these checks when changing qconfig or cache policy:
  1) Unit tests: automated response-length and tokenization parity checks.
  2) Offline eval: sample prompt set, compute task-specific metrics (F1, BLEU, ROUGE, embedding cosine shift). Set acceptance thresholds (e.g., embedding cosine > 0.98 vs baseline).
  3) Shadow traffic run for 12–48 hours with logging for divergences.
  4) Canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% with automatic rollback on quality regression or p95 latency spikes.

Experiment log template (copy into sheets)
- experiment_id:
- start_ts / end_ts:
- workload_profile:
- model + baseline qconfig:
- new qconfig / batching / cache settings:
- sample_size (tokens, requests) collected:
- latency metrics (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1M tokens baseline vs variant:
- quality metrics (task-specific): baseline vs variant delta:
- notes / observed regressions:

Recent experiment highlights (summary)
- exp-2025-11-03 (L2-13B, chat): awq8 reduced GPU memory by ~36% and lowered token compute cost by 28% with a 0.8% increase in perplexity on our conversational check set. p95 latency +12ms at battarget 6 — acceptable for non-low-latency tiers.
- exp-2025-12-10 (embeddings pipeline): batched embedding forward (32) + int8 quantization reduced cost-per-vector by 58% and median latency improved due to batch amortization; observed a 0.6% drop in nearest-neighbor MRR on benchmark dataset.
- exp-2026-01-18 (long-context summarization): enabling KV offload cut OOM errors for 32k token windows and reduced failed-request rate from 2.3% -> 0.5%; tail latency increased by ~80ms but throughput stability improved.

Operational playbook snippets
- If p95 latency spikes after increasing battarget: reduce battarget by 1 and reduce max_queue_ms by 5ms; re-evaluate.
- If quality regression appears after qconfig change: immediately revert to previous qconfig and run offline regression tests; promote change only if shadow runs are clean.
- For cache invalidation bugs: add cache-key tracing to request logs and correlate with user session IDs; prefer TTL-based eviction over manual invalidation unless session semantics require it.

Cost model quick math (back-of-envelope)
- baseline: baseline_tokens_per_sec * cost_per_token = baseline_cost
- batching effect: effective_cost_per_token ≈ baseline_cost_per_token / batching_efficiency_factor (observe empirically; common range 1.2–2.4 improvement)
- quantization effect: q_cost_factor ≈ 0.4–0.75 depending on qconfig and kernel impl
- combined: expect multiplicative but non-linear gains; always measure end-to-end.

Open questions / things to try next
- Evaluate AWQ/QLoRA hybrids on 70B families with large chat workloads for stability vs latency tradeoffs.
- Automated battarget tuner in Runtime: dynamic adjustment based on recent p95 and queue length.
- Cache sharding heuristics to minimize KV-copy overhead for multi-tenant inference.
- Explore hardware-aware qconfig selection at routing time: route to int8 pool when quality budget available and fp16 when not.

Next steps (owner: Priya)
- Convert experiment log template into a shared sheet and hook to the Optimize dashboard (due 2026-03-15).
- Run two 72-hour canaries using recommended defaults for small-chat and embeddings (owners: Miguel, Ethan).
- Draft a condensed one-pager for SRE runbooks with rollback steps (owner: Lina).

Notes / references:
- See linked artifacts for relevant PRs and tickets.
- Keep this doc lightweight; file a longer playbook only after 2–3 successful canaries.
